silhouette.model: perspective oblate spheroid fitted on limb rays
silhouette.note: the painted globe is clearly oblate, so the silhouette is an oblate spheroid with the pole on the ring normal

camera.note: three.js PerspectiveCamera, looks down local -Z; identity rotation, so world axes are the camera axes and world +Y is image up

rings.note: inner and outer are the edges of the bright rings at blurred luminance 0.25; the faint C ring inside and the thin outer ringlet beyond are not included

sunFit.model: luminance = ambient + gain * max(0, n.s), soft L1, plus n.s = 0 on the detected terminator

moons.depthFrom: orbit radius 20 body radii, back side

globe.note: pole on the ring normal, north toward the visible pole at the top

conventions.globeLocal: direction of (lon, lat) is (cos(lat) sin(lon), sin(lat), cos(lat) cos(lon)); lon 0 lat 0 is local +Z; world = quaternion * (scale * local)
conventions.map: equirectangular, u = lon/360 + 0.5, v = lat/180 + 0.5, north at the top
conventions.threeSphereGeometry: SphereGeometry puts u at (-cos(2 pi u) sin(theta), cos(theta), sin(2 pi u) sin(theta)): u = 0.5 is +X and east runs counterclockwise about +Y seen from the north, the same handedness as the local frame above. The map is not mirrored and needs no flip; it is only turned 90 degrees about Y, so on a SphereGeometry mesh use meshQuaternionForThreeSphereGeometry (globe.quaternion times a -90 degree turn about Y) and globe.scale

refit.sun: grid search of the globe's shadow on the rings against the hero (assets-src/saturn/rings/fit_sun.py): overlap 0.79, was 0.48 with the Sun fitted on the terminator alone
refit.normal: ring edges straightest in the polar view (assets-src/saturn/rings/fit_plane.py): edge wander 0.038 radii rms, was 0.060
